The `--settle-ms 50` in inspect.int.test.ts:123 is an argument passed to the script under test, not a sleep in the test. skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs:87 Precondition: a file has an `export` or `import` statement with no `from` clause, as in `export const App = ...` or `export function f() {}`. The repo style has no semicolons, and a later line has `import type { T } from './t'`, or a mid-file import. Trace: the clause group `([^'\";]*?)` is lazy but may span newlines and cannot stop at a statement boundary. So `export` matches, the clause grows across lines until it reaches `from '...'`, and the captured clause becomes e.g. `const x = 1\\nimport type { T }`. Because the `type\\s+` check applies only right after the leading keyword, `typeOnly` is false. The inline-type check fails too, because `names` is undefined for a clause that does not start with `{`. Failure: a type-only import is recorded as a runtime import, and `registryIsRouted` can report the registry as routed when it is not. This is the false positive the change was meant to remove. Uncertain: how often it happens in real hosts; it needs a semicolon-free `export` before a later `import ... from`.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs:93 Precondition: index.html contains a commented-out module script, such as `<!-- <script type=\"module\" src=\"/src/old-main.tsx\"></script> -->`. Trace: `htmlEntries` scans the raw HTML with a regex and does not strip comments. Before this change only the first script tag was considered. Now every module script is an entry point, so commented-out or stale scripts are also traced. Failure: if a commented-out entry imports the registry, `registryIsRouted` returns true and the index anchor is treated as satisfied. The scaffold then skips telling the user to route the registry, which is a silent false positive.\n\n━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\nTotal: 2 fixed, 0 skipped, 0 failed after 2 That fact does not leave the clause &quot;every wait for preview readiness has a timeout&quot; unmet. The readiness wait is the `for (;;)` loop, and it has an explicit timeout. tiebreaks{"demo-integration":null,"scene-kit":null,"presentation-skill":null,"verification-tooling":{"ok":true,"criteria":["verification-step-error-fails"],"inventory_kind":"neutral source","attempts":[{"stage":"tiebreak","attempt":1,"ok":true,"error":null}],"first_results":[{"id":"verification-step-error-fails","verdict":"fail","rationale":"The guidance says the verifier must not treat a missing or non-numeric data-step-index as progress. It also says to fail when the transition check turns a non-numeric hook into a number that still passes its comparison, giving Number(null) === 0 on the first step as the example. In scripts/verify.mjs, readStep finds the root with document.querySelector(&#39;[data-step-index]&#39;). That selector matches an element whose attribute is present but empty. readStep then sets index to Number(root.getAttribute(&#39;data-step-index&#39;)), and Number(&#39;&#39;) is 0. The first-step check on line 108 accepts `observed.index === 0` with no check that the hook holds a real number. So an empty, non-numeric data-step-index on step 1 passes the first-step comparison. This is the same coercion the guidance names as a fail condition. Judge B&#39;s reason is borne out by these lines and decides the requirement. I rule A and B&#39;s pass. Judge C fails the criterion because `STEP_SETTLE_MS` in verify.mjs and `settleMs` in inspect add fixed settle delays. (1) Bounded readiness: `startPreview` in both common.mjs copies sets `deadline = Date.now() + 20000`. It polls `fetch(origin)` every 100ms, stops the child and throws once the deadline passes, and also throws if the child exits. The page-level readiness waits also have explicit timeouts: `waitForSelector` with 10000 in verify and inspect, `waitForFunction` with 3000 in verify, and 5000 in inspect. (2) Build before preview: `verify()` awaits `run(&#39;npm&#39;,[&#39;run&#39;,&#39;build&#39;])` and throws on a non-zero exit before calling `startPreview`. `inspect()` does the same whenever it builds. (3) Readiness comes from an HTTP probe, not from parsing the server&#39;s printed ready URL, so the ANSI/chunk-splitting clause does not apply. The template copies have the same code. I rule A and B&#39;s pass. Judge C fails the criterion because the individual `await fetch` has no abort signal, so the 20s deadline is only checked after each fetch settles. The cited loop does have a timeout on the readiness wait, though. C&#39;s point depends on a server that accepts the connection but never answers. The candidate does not produce that scenario and the review guidance does not name it. That promise resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event (helpers.ts:46-55), which is observable process state. The tests then assert on the exit code, the output and the files written. The one wait loop in a test is `gone(pid)` (helpers.ts:66-74). It polls `alive(pid)` against a deadline and returns as soon as the state changes, so it is a polling wait. Every fixed timer in the test tree serves another purpose. inspect.int.test.ts:64 is inside a generated fixture Scene&#39;s useEffect and simulates content that settles late in the app under test; no test waits on it. verify-script.test.ts:165 is inside a fake-page stub&#39;s `goto`, which makes a fake error arrive late; no browser is involved. In inspect-script.test.ts:159-162, `sleep` is an injected fake that only records events and advances a fake clock. A grep for setTimeout, waitForTimeout and sleep across tests/ and src/**/*.test.* finds only these occurrences and the gone() poll. The jsdom component tests wait on DOM state with `waitFor` and `findByText` (Stage.test.tsx:65-76, Router.test.tsx:38-48). No test treats an immediate call such as reading an element count as a wait. Judge A (pass) and Judge B (pass) are consistent with this source. Judge C (fail) points out that verify&#39;s renderSteps and inspect&#39;s captureSteps wait a fixed settle interval inside the scripts. Those delays belong to the verification scripts under test, not to the tests. The criterion asks whether the browser tests sleep instead of waiting for state. These tests wait on child-process close and poll process liveness, and none waits a fixed time before asserting. The `--settle-ms 50` in inspect.int.test.ts:123 is an argument passed to the script under test, not a sleep in the test. The review guidance also says longer fixed settle delays earn neither credit nor failure. None of them sleeps for a fixed time before asserting. Each one launches verify or inspect through `exec()` in helpers.ts. That promise resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event (helpers.ts:46-55), which is observable process state. The tests then assert on the exit code, the output and the files written. The one wait loop in a test is `gone(pid)` (helpers.ts:66-74). It polls `alive(pid)` against a deadline and returns as soon as the state changes, so it is a polling wait. Every fixed timer in the test tree serves another purpose. inspect.int.test.ts:64 is inside a generated fixture Scene&#39;s useEffect and simulates content that settles late in the app under test; no test waits on it. verify-script.test.ts:165 is inside a fake-page stub&#39;s `goto`, which makes a fake error arrive late; no browser is involved. In inspect-script.test.ts:159-162, `sleep` is an injected fake that only records events and advances a fake clock. A grep for setTimeout, waitForTimeout and sleep across tests/ and src/**/*.test.* finds only these occurrences and the gone() poll. The jsdom component tests wait on DOM state with `waitFor` and `findByText` (Stage.test.tsx:65-76, Router.test.tsx:38-48). No test treats an immediate call such as reading an element count as a wait. Judge A (pass) and Judge B (pass) are consistent with this source. Judge C (fail) points out that verify&#39;s renderSteps and inspect&#39;s captureSteps wait a fixed settle interval inside the scripts. Those delays belong to the verification scripts under test, not to the tests. The criterion asks whether the browser tests sleep instead of waiting for state. These tests wait on child-process close and poll process liveness, and none waits a fixed time before asserting. The `--settle-ms 50` in inspect.int.test.ts:123 is an argument passed to the script under test, not a sleep in the test. The review guidance also says longer fixed settle delays earn neither credit nor failure. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-clear-code-boundaries","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The auditor&#39;s argument is that writing the title to a data attribute counts as consuming it, even if nothing reads the attribute. The guidance asks for the title to be traced through the demo, and the check fails if the public title contract is ignored rather than consumed. The supplied source shows that Talk passes the title. Presentation then writes it only to `data-presentation-title-text` on the root div. The material shows no other use of the title. It is not rendered as visible text, not set as the document title, and not used as an accessible name. Header shows only the brand, the step number and the era. Footer&#39;s h2 shows `step.title`, not the presentation title. A value that ends up only in a non-semantic data attribute has no visible or functional effect. Under the plain meaning of a presentation title, that is ignored, not consumed. A data attribute alone does not meet the title contract. The auditor&#39;s other point, that the rest of the code is well organised, does not answer this specific reason for the fail.","evidence":["Presentation.tsx declares `title?: string` and destructures it. Its only use is `data-presentation-title-text={title}` on the root div.","Footer.tsx renders `&lt;h2 data-presentation-title=&quot;&quot;&gt;{step.title}&lt;/h2&gt;`. This is the per-step title, not the presentation title.","Header.tsx renders the brand, the step number and `step.era`. It never receives or renders the presentation title.","Talk.tsx passes `title=&quot;How to Use This Skill to Make a Presentation&quot;`. In the supplied material, that value never becomes visible or accessible output."],"citations":["src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx","src/presentation-kit/chrome/Footer.tsx","src/presentation-kit/chrome/Header.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":1,"sample":2}],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
